items.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
items.summary: OpenAI released two new models, GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, aimed at professional work, coding and 3D design while cutting Astra's standard API price by 20% to $8 per million input tokens. The launch comes seven weeks after OpenAI reportedly scrapped a planned GPT-6.1 Astra over an alignment regression found in safety testing.

items.headline: Microsoft reinvents Copilot as an autonomous enterprise agent at Ignite 2026
items.summary: At its Ignite conference, Microsoft unveiled Autopilot, an always-on cloud-based Copilot agent that keeps work moving without step-by-step direction, alongside expansions to the Cowork task-delegation portal and Agent 365's AI-budgeting tools. The push signals Microsoft's bet on autonomous agents as the next phase of enterprise AI competition against Google and Meta.

items.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns; CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO
items.summary: Nvidia announced that Jensen Huang stepped down immediately as president, CEO and board member after 33 years, with CFO Colette Kress taking over as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor. Shares fell roughly 10% in pre-market trading amid reports linking the exit to a personal-conduct inquiry, which the board said found no evidence company or national-security information was compromised.

items.headline: Nvidia halts Hopper-class AI chip shipments to China despite US approval
items.summary: Interim CEO Colette Kress told investors on an earnings call that Nvidia's guidance excludes licensed Hopper-generation data-center chips for China going forward, after selling $2.4 billion of them in the prior quarter, even though Washington had eased licensing earlier in the year. Nvidia also created a new board-level export-control oversight committee the same week, while its more advanced Blackwell and Rubin chips remain barred from the Chinese market entirely.

items.headline: Meta releases Muse Ember, its smallest and cheapest AI model, for agent workloads
items.summary: Meta Superintelligence Labs launched Muse Ember, a lightweight model priced at $0.10/$0.50 per million input/output tokens and designed to handle high-volume agent execution tasks like tool calls and document parsing while a larger Muse model plans the work. It's the latest step in Meta's pivot away from open-weight Llama releases toward its closed Muse model family.

items.headline: Anthropic publishes new prompting guidance for Claude Opus 5.5
items.summary: Anthropic released an updated prompting guide advising developers to drop legacy instructions like "think step by step" for Claude Opus 5.5, which generates tokens over 30% faster and often finishes tasks with fewer tokens than Opus 5. The guide also notes that extended thinking can no longer be disabled on Opus 5.5 at higher effort levels, which can affect apps relying on fixed output caps.

items.headline: Boston Dynamics expands Spot deployment and begins Atlas testing at GlobalFoundries
items.summary: Boston Dynamics and chipmaker GlobalFoundries expanded their robotics partnership, with Spot robots taking on asset-management work across GF's semiconductor fabs in New York, Vermont, Germany and Singapore while the humanoid Atlas begins trials there too. It's part of Boston Dynamics' push to move Atlas beyond automotive plants, with all of its 2026 production capacity already committed to customers including Hyundai and Google DeepMind.

items.headline: Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid lands its first non-automotive industrial trial
items.summary: Atlas, Boston Dynamics' production humanoid robot built initially for automotive manufacturing floors, has started its first trial deployment outside the auto industry, broadening the commercial case for humanoid labor in general industrial settings. The move follows a leadership change at the company, which named former Amazon executive Rohit Prasad as CEO earlier this fall.

items.headline: Agility Robotics goes public as the first US-listed humanoid robotics maker
items.summary: Agility Robotics completed a business combination to begin trading publicly, becoming the first specialist humanoid robotics company listed on a US exchange, entering the market with more than $300 million in conditional multiyear orders for its Digit 5 humanoid. The listing follows Agility's recent commercial deployment agreement with manufacturer AGCO.

items.headline: Edge0 open-sources a 145-billion-parameter model that runs on a single laptop GPU
items.summary: Startup Edge0 released Edge0-145B and a smaller Edge0-120B, billed as the first open-source on-device models at that scale, claiming they can run on a consumer laptop with roughly 29GB of peak memory or a single 16GB consumer GPU. The model is built on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, with weights on Hugging Face and an Apache-2.0 inference framework on GitHub, though performance figures are the vendor's own and not yet independently verified.
